enacted on March 27, 2020, to be used to exclusively on eligible activities that prevent
and respond to the COVID-19 pandemic.
CDBG-CV funding was allocated to eligible activities including South Antelope Valley
Emergency Services (SAVES), Business Public Service, Economic Opportunity
Programs, Mortgage Assistance, Rental Assistance and Administration of the grant
funding.
In addition, SAVES received an allocation of Community Development Block Grant
funds for the 2022-2023 Program Year for operations of the SAVES Program.

DISCUSSION

SAVES has continued to provide increased services to the community since the COVID
emergency was initiated. Currently SAVES is providing 1,000 to 1,800 food orders
weekly. Due to the high level of service provided by SAVES and increased costs for a
period of time longer than anticipated when funding was initially provided, SAVES is
requesting an increase of $180,000 funding, increasing funding from $575,010 to
$755,010.
The Emergency Rental Assistance (COVID) Program (ERAP) has an interest list of 344
households. Under ERAP rental assistance of up to a total of $10,000 for up to six
consecutive months may be provided to eligible households. Housing Division Staff has
requested additional funding of $178,000 increasing CDBG-CV funding from $300,000 to
$478,000.
The Mortgage Assistance Program has determined 7 households may be eligible for
assistance and have been provided applications. Under this program an eligible
household’s payment assistance may be up to a total of $6,000 for up to six consecutive
months. Funding of $42,000 is allocated for these applicants. Loans in forbearance are
not eligible for assistance due to not being delinquent. The Mortgage Assistance Program
CDBG-CV allocation available for reprogramming is $258,000.
The CDBG-CV grant provides 20% of the allocation for Administration of the grant.
Administration funds of $239,600 are currently available. Staff is utilizing Administration
funding for processing program applications to maximize the funding available for direct
program assistance and determined $100,000 may be reprogrammed for ERAP
assistance.
The requested reprogramming of CDBG-CV funds is a non-substantial amendment to the
2019-2020 Action Plan in accordance with the approved Citizen Participation Plan.
Budget transfers are requested for SAVES CDBG-CV to allocate funding for operations
accounts. Budget transfers are requested for SAVES to allocate funding for operations
accounts. SAVES CDBG approved funding for Program Year 2022-2023 is $217,917 and

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2023-023, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE AUTHORIZING THE
  EXECUTION OF A SURETY BOND TO MEET THE FINANCIAL
  SECURITY REQUIREMENT FOR ENERGY FOR PALMDALE’S
  INDEPENDENT CHOICE

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-023, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale authorizing the execution of a Surety Bond to meet the financial security
requirement for Energy for Palmdale’s Independent Choice.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-023 authorizing
the execution of a surety bond to meet the Financial Security Requirement for EPIC.

BACKGROUND
On April 2, 2019, City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1524 establishing the Palmdale
Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) program, Energy for Palmdale’s Independent
Choice (EPIC). EPIC began serving electricity to customers in October 2022. EPIC’s
mission is to provide the benefits of clean, renewable energy while achieving greater
local control over electricity services, promoting competitively priced renewable energy
options, and providing quality programs and services to the local community.

DISCUSSION
In 2018, the CPUC issued Decision 18-05-022 (Decision) which established reentry fees
and Financial Security Requirements (FSR) for CCAs. The purpose of the FSR
instrument is to cover reentry fees borne by the Investor Owned Utility (IOU) in the event
of a mass involuntary return of CCA customers to the IOU, such as a decertification of
a CCA or a CCA failure. The IOU may only withhold funds from the financial security
instrument for unpaid administrative or procurement costs associated with the return of
CCA customers to the IOU. Any withholding of those funds must first be approved by
the CPUC.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-023 Authorizing the execution of a surety bond to
meet the Financial Security Requirement for Energy for Palmdale’s Independent Choice
April 5, 2023
Page 2

The Decision required all CCAs, including EPIC, to submit an Advice Letter with the FSR
instrument to the CPUC to show compliance with the Decision. The City’s CCA
consultants, California Choice Energy Authority (CalChoice), worked with its legal team
to draft the advice letter, which was submitted with a copy of an executed Letter of
Credit, which was the instrument used to satisfy the FSR obligation. The FSR amount
has been $147,000 since the initial posting of the Letter of Credit in 2021. The Letter of
Credit, issued by River City Bank (RCB), is collateralized by a cash deposit of $147,000
in an account held with RCB in the City’s name.

The methodology used to calculate the FSR amount for CCAs is under review at the
CPUC to ensure that IOUs do not unreasonably bear costs associated with CCA
customer returns to the IOU. In anticipation of a change to the methodology to calculate
the FSR amount which may result in an increase in the FSR amount, staff is proposing
replacing the current Letter of Credit, which requires dollar-for-dollar cash collateral, with
a surety bond, which is more flexible and has an approximate one percent (1%) annual
fee. Because the methodology used to calculate the FSR includes benchmarks related
to energy pricing, which can move up and down depending on market conditions, staff
is requesting a not to exceed amount that contemplates future volatility in the energy
market. Currently, the estimated fee for the first year is less than $2,000. When the
current Letter of Credit expires, the $147,000 cash collateral will be released to the City.

Based on the foregoing, staff recommends the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2023-
023 authorizing the execution of a surety bond and related documents for the purpose
of satisfying the Financial Security Requirement as required by the California Public
Utilities Commission.

FISCAL IMPACT
Fees for FY 2022-2023 are approximated around $2,000 and have already been
budgeted for in account 35034003-721411. Staff is requesting a not to exceed amount
that contemplates future volatility in the energy market and is not to exceed $25,000,
annually. Sufficient revenues will be generated by EPIC to cover operating expenses,
including surety bond fees.

  BACKGROUND

  At the September 2, 2020, City Council meeting, the City Council approved Ordinance
  No. 1550, adding Chapter 2.55 to the Palmdale Municipal Code creating the Palmdale
  Human Rights Advisory Committee (“Committee”). Under Ordinance No. 1550, the
  Committee was created by the City Council to act in an advisory capacity to the Mayor,
  City Council and City Manager. The Committee would provide advice and actionable
  recommendations to the Mayor, City Council and City Manager in their efforts to build
  and maintain an inclusive community by cultivating awareness, increasing diversity,
  encouraging sensitivity, promoting equity, and improving relations with various
  segments of the community. Residency in the City of Palmdale is not required.

DISCUSSION
The terms for the current Human Rights Advisory Committee Members expire April
2023. City Council directed staff to open a recruitment for the Human Rights Advisory
Committee. A recruitment advertisement was placed in the AV Press for interested
citizens to apply. The Communications Division also provided a press release to the
public, including the application submittal deadline, and posted the advertisement on the
city’s Social Media pages. The Classified Ad and the application were made available
on the Board & Commission webpage and the HRAC webpage, as well as in the Office
of the City Clerk. Staff received twelve (12) applications by the March 9, 2023, 6:00 p.m.
deadline.

Appointments to the Human Rights Advisory Committee are made according to
2.08.030(C) & (D), All such applications shall be provided to the City Council for review,
who shall, at a regularly scheduled City Council meeting, nominate, from among such
applicants, the persons whom the City Councilmembers desire to appoint by making a
motion for each such appointment. If the nomination is approved by a majority vote of
the City Council, the nominating City Councilmember may then proceed to appoint the
person to the board or commission under consideration.

 Dear Human Rights Advisory Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Human Rights Advisory Committee position and am honored to
apply for a position on your committee. As an immigrant from Indonesia, I have experienced
discrimination, abuse, and financial hardship throughout my life. These experiences have given me a
unique perspective on the importance of protecting the human rights of marginalized communities,
including those who face challenges related to education, housing, employment, race relations, social
equity, LGBTQ rights, gender equality, civil rights, and the rights of any other minority or historically
marginalized communities.

My personal journey has inspired me to become an advocate for those who face similar challenges. As a
woman who has experienced sexual, physical, and mental abuse, I understand the importance of creating
safe spaces for survivors of trauma. Additionally, as someone who has faced discrimination within the
math and engineering fields, I understand the importance of promoting diversity and inclusion in all areas
of education and employment.

Growing up in a chaotic and abusive home, gave me an insight on the importance of safe and affordable
housing for all individuals. My family struggled to put food on the table, and we often had to rely on food
banks and community resources to survive. This experience has given me a deep appreciation for the
importance of access to basic needs, such as food and shelter.

Furthermore, my family has also faced mental health challenges, including schizophrenia and bipolar
disorder. My sister, who was born a lesbian, has also faced challenges navigating the world as a member
of the LGBTQ community. Witnessing these struggles has given me a unique perspective on the
importance of promoting mental health awareness and advocating for the rights of the LGBTQ
community.

In my professional life, I have served as a Software Project Manager and as the Regional Vice President
of Technology for Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society. Through my volunteer work with organizations such
as Women Who Code and Data Con LA, I have also gained valuable experience working with diverse
groups of people and advocating for the rights of marginalized communities.

I am committed to using my professional and personal experiences to make a difference in my community
and beyond. I believe that my unique perspective and diverse background make me well-suited for a
position on your committee. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

  ORDINANCE NO. 1550

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  ADDING CHAPTER 2,55 TO THE PALMDALE MUNICIPAL CODE
  CREATING THE PALMDALE HUMAN RIGHTS ADVISORY COMMITTEE

  WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Palmdale desires to establish the
Palmdale Human Rights Advisory Committee to promote continued dialogue with
various segments of the community in the hopes of building and maintaining a more
inclusive community; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council discussed and agreed to move forward with the
creation of a Human Rights Advisory Committee at the August 4th Council meet¡ng.

THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. A new Chapter 2.55, entitled "Palmdale Human Rights Advisory
Committee" is added to the Palmdale Municipal Code to read as follows:

  Chapter 2.55
  Palmdale Human Rights Advisory Committee

  2.55.010. Establishment and Purpose. A Human Rights Advisory Commiitee
  is created by the City Council of the City of Palmdale to act in an advisory
  capacity to the Mayor, City Council and City Manager. The purpose of the
  Palmdale Human Rights Advisory Committee is to provide advice and
  actionable recommendations to the Mayor, City Council and City Manager in
  their effods to build and maintain an inclusive community by cultivating
  awareness, increasing diversity, encouraging sensitivity, promoting equity, and
  improving relations with various segments of the community.

  2.55.020. Membership. The Palmdale Human Rights Advisory Committee shall
  have seven (7) Members. All Committee Members shall be appointed
  pursuant to Section 2.08.030 of the Palmdale Municipal Code.
 Ordinance No. 1550
Page 2 of 3

  2.55.030. Term of Office. The term of each Committee Member shall be two
  (2) years, commencing on the date of appointment. A Committee Member may
  be reappointed for additional terms. All Committee Members serve at the
  pleasure of the Mayor and Clty Council. Any vacancy on the Committee shall
  be filled pursuant to Section 2.08.030 of the Palmdale Municipal Code.

  2,55.040. Qualifications. The Mayor and Council shall strive to approve
  Committee Members with experience in any of the following areas: education;
  housing; employment; race relations; social equity; lesbian, gay, bisexual,
  transgender, and queer (LGBTO) rights; gender equality; civil rights; and the
  rights of any other minority or historically marginalized communities.
